highlights: SOTO transfers KLTs between warehouse and production with a conveyor gripper, three-sided pickup and configurable backpack. Capacity 8–24 totes depends on tote size; 24 totes at 20 kg each is not a permitted 480 kg load.

Handling limit is 20 kg per tote. Total transport load differs: Magazino 250 kg; Jungheinrich UK240 kg; December 2023 technical sheet 200–249 kg by backpack and 240 kg standard, with its load-carrier row also specifying 240 kg total.

The December 2023 sheet gives 686–735 kg own mass by backpack (695 kg standard), 2230×1060×2160 mm body dimensions plus 80 mm operating laser-scanner height, IP20 and indoor industrial-floor conditions. These are revision/configuration-qualified manufacturer data.

Omnidirectional drive reaches up to 1.5 m/s. Minimum aisle 1650 mm is associated with 0.3 m/s; maximum-speed aisle is 2500 mm on Magazino’s page versus 2510 mm in the sheet. The stated 3100 mm minimum turning circle is not a turning-radius value.

Magazino gives 0.4–1.7 m tote transfer height; the sheet distinguishes minimum 500 mm frontal versus 400 mm lateral gripping height and 1700 mm maximum. These are gripper heights rather than fork height, stroke or arm reach.

Up to 8 h between charges is manufacturer-rated. UK page states 1.5 h charging versus 1.6 h in the December 2023 sheet; 5:1 drive/charge ratio lacks stated start/end charge levels. WMS/REST and VDA5050 integration do not establish a protocol version, independent safety certification or guaranteed fleet performance.

fields.description: TORU is Magazino’s autonomous mobile picking robot for shoeboxes and supported standardized KLTs, using a vacuum gripper, lifting column and onboard backpack. The product page specifies up to 5.8 kg per gripped object and a 390×280×145 mm maximum object envelope, with up to 16 objects transported and 0.08–2.5 m action height. The February 6, 2025 NEO system article instead limits loaded KLTs to 5 kg, contents to 380×240×140 mm and picking height to 2.2 m for that application. NEO buffer stations, a separate cobot and 350+picks/hour belong to the integrated system. Up to 20 hours/day operation does not establish battery endurance, and object dimensions are not chassis dimensions.

highlights: TORU picks and returns individual shoeboxes or supported special KLTs using a vacuum gripper on a lifting column. The product page permits gripped objects up to 5.8 kg and 390×280×145 mm (L×W×H); these are object limits, not robot mass or chassis dimensions.

The product page specifies up to 16 objects in its backpack and an action range 0.08–2.5 m above the floor. Sixteen objects is a count, not proof of a 92.8 kg total transport rating or a 2.5 m radial arm reach.

The February 6, 2025 NEO application combines TORUs, standardized totes, an automated buffer, a separate goods-to-employee cobot and operating software. It states loaded KLT limit 5 kg, content envelope 380×240×140 mm and picking height up to 2.2 m; those application limits remain separate from the general TORU page.

NEO350+picks/hour, more-than 3000 picks/day suitability, pay-per-pick terms and 6–8 week implementation describe the integrated system/business offer, not an independently measured one-robot throughput, TORU price or guaranteed ROI.

ARC fleet control connects to warehouse management over WLAN and exposes maps, orders and assistance. Up-to 20 hours/day operation, generic 24/7 positioning and remote monitoring 24 hours/6 days per week are distinct schedules rather than one-charge endurance or a charge duration.

SOTO moves totes with a conveyor gripper and configurable multi-load backpack; TORU uses vacuum gripping of supported shoeboxes or KLTs. Product handling loads, backpack counts and configuration-specific total payloads retain different meanings.

Magazino’s SOTO Fleet Manager/WMS and VDA5050 integration and TORU ARC fleet tools provide planning, monitoring and assistance. These functions do not establish an exact supported VDA5050 protocol revision or independent performance/safety results.

The February 2025 NEO application integrates TORUs with separate buffers, a cobot workstation and software under a pay-per-pick offer. Integrated-system throughput, economic/labor outcomes, safety language and manufacturer exclusivity claims are not independently verified robot ratings.
